decision_titles: Treasurer's report, $60,703,419.85 expenditures, and indemnification contracts
plain_text:
MANCHESTER SCHOOL DISTRICT SAU #37 
COMMITTEE ON FINANCE & FACILITIES 
 
August 12, 2026 6:00 p.m. 
 
1. Chairman O’Connell called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. 
 
2. The Clerk called the roll.  
 
Present: Committee Members O’Connell, Turner, Potter, and Hamer. 
Absent: Committee Member Parr. 
 
 
3. PUBLIC COMMENT 
 
There was no one present wishing to speak. 
 
 
4.  Approval of minutes from June 10, 2026, Finance & Facilities meeting.    
 
On motion of Committee Member Turner, duly seconded by Committee Member Hamer, it was 
moved to approve the minutes of the June 10, 2026 Finance and Facilities Meetings.  All were in favor 
and the motion passed.  
 
 
5. CONSENT AGENDA 
 
Committee Member Turner removed item c and Committee Chair O’Connell removed item b from the 
consent agenda for discussion. 
 
On motion of Committee Member Potter, duly seconded by Committee Member Turner, it was moved 
to approve the balance of the consent agenda as submitted.  All present were in favor and the motion 
passed.  
 
When approving the consent agenda items, the recommendations put forward from the administration 
is what the board is approving and those recommendations are included below.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 2 of 11 
 
  
a. Treasurer’s Report – by Freda Hawkinson, Treasurer     
 
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve the Treasurer’s Report as submitted and 
forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval.   
 
 
b.  Removed from the consent agenda for discussion, see below. 
 
 
c.  Removed from the consent agenda for discussion, see below. 
 
 
d. Manifest of Authorized Expenditures - June and July 2026 – by Karen     
DeFrancis, Executive Director of Finance ($60,703,419.85) 
 
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve the Manifest of Expenditures for June and 
July 2026, in the amount of $60,703,419.85, and forward this item to the Board of School Committee 
for approval.   
    
 
e. Indemnification Contract Language – by Karen DeFrancis,  Executive     
Director of Finance 
 
The Committee on Finance and Facilities moved to approve the indemnification contract language for 
Lincoln National Life Insurance Company; Easter Seals New Hampshire Inc.; Soliant Health, LLC; 
Saint Anselm College for Prom, the Department of Nursing and Social Work Practicum; Franklin 
Pierce University; Lindamood-Bell Learning Processes; Seven Hills New Hampshire; and the Pine 
Haven Boys Center, and forward this item to the Board of School Committee for approval.  
 
 
b. Grants, Gifts & Donations Report – by Polly Golden, Grant Manager    
($6,365,856.09)  
 
Chair O’Connell explained that Item 5B required a separate motion because it included the scheduling 
of a public hearing.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 3 of 11 
 
  
On motion of Committee Member Potter, duly seconded by Committee Member Turner, it was moved 
to approve, with gratitude, the Grants, Gifts and Donations report, in the amount of $6,365,856.09, 
and forward this item to the full Board of School Committee for approval and to schedule a public 
hearing on the donation of $28,300 from The Break Room of 138 musical instruments. All present were 
in favor and the motion passed.  
 
c. City Service Invoices – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director of  Finance   
($2,020,688.76) 
 
Committee Member Turner raised several questions regarding the City Services documentation.  They 
included: 
1. Regarding the Aramark invoices appearing on pages 54 and 56 of the agenda packet, she asked 
whether the figures had been reviewed and verified, noting that the multiple crossed-out 
amounts made the invoices difficult to follow.  Mrs. DeFrancis confirmed that the invoices had 
been reviewed and compared with the budget. She explained that Aramark submits a monthly 
invoice to the City, after which the costs are separated between the City and School District. 
Under the previous contract, the services were included under one contract, with preventive 
maintenance and custodial costs also requiring allocation. She stated that each month she 
verifies the District's portion against the contract, confirms the City/School allocation agrees 
with the total invoice, and ensures the District's costs are appropriate. She also explained that 
approximately $100,000 is retained annually, or approximately $8,333 per month, and paid at 
the end of the year. She confirmed that the invoices, including the retainage, reconcile with the 
amount budgeted.  
2. She then questioned the $28,594.81 athletics maintenance charge associated with Gill Stadium. 
Administration explained that only $539.10 of that amount was specifically for Gill Stadium 
lighting. Approximately $14,149.99 shown on a subsequent page included soccer goals and a 
bulk purchase of weed killer and fertilizer sufficient for approximately one year. The remaining 
amount reflected other Parks and Recreation work. Administration noted that the total shown 
on page 72, $28,594.81, matched the amount reported on page 66. 
3. Committee Member Turner expressed frustration with the difficulty of interpreting the monthly 
invoices and stated that she would continue asking questions when charges appeared unclear. 
Administration indicated that the City was transitioning to the Tyler Munis system and 
expressed hope that future invoices would be more user-friendly.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 4 of 11 
 
  
4. She also asked why Parks and Recreation chargeback reports appeared more than once for the 
same months. Administration explained that the reports are intentionally separated between 
school grounds/general maintenance and athletics because the athletics budget is tracked 
separately. A summary page provides monthly totals for each category. 
5. Committee Member Turner requested that Wilson be removed from the reports if it was no 
longer necessary for it to appear. Administration agreed to make the request. 
 
Chair O’Connell questioned a $2,804 charge for St. Anthony’s Field. Administration explained that the 
District uses St. Anthony’s Field for middle school athletics, including soccer in the fall and softball in 
the spring, with softball activities serving the District's four middle schools.  
 
On motion of Committee Member Turner, duly seconded by Committee Member Potter, it was moved 
to approve the City Services Invoices, in the amount of $2,020,688.76, and forward this item to the 
Board of School Committee for approval. All present were in favor and the motion passed.  
 
               
6. ACTION AGENDA 
  
a. Financial Reports – by Karen DeFrancis, Executive Director of Finance    
 
Mrs. DeFrancis presented the year-end financial reports. She reported that General Fund expenditures 
were coming in close to the projections presented to the Committee in June. The salary line was projected 
to end with an approximately $1.5 million surplus, attributable primarily to lower-than-budgeted driver 
costs, special education staffing shortages that resulted in services being provided through contracted 
services, and other vacant positions during the year.  Health insurance was projected to end 
approximately $2 million over budget based on actual costs. Although the report reflected an 
approximately $4 million variance, $2 million of that amount resulted from the budget assumption that 
$2 million would be used to support the budget. Final year-end entries, including pharmacy rebates, were 
still pending.  Special education contracted services and tuition were approximately $2.6 million over 
budget, an improvement from the approximately $3 million overage projected in May. Mrs. DeFrancis 
noted that final purchase orders and bills had reduced the projected overage.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 5 of 11 
 
  
As previously approved by the Board of School Committee, the District would utilize $886,000 from the 
Teaching and Learning Trust for curriculum and $400,000 from the same trust for Chromebooks 
purchased during the prior year.  Mrs. DeFrancis also reported a reduction in specialized transportation 
costs compared with the prior year.  
 
General Fund revenues finished stronger than anticipated. Significant favorable variances included: 
 Special education revenue approximately $667,000 above budget;  
 Interest revenue approximately $273,000 above budget;  
 Medicaid revenue approximately $464,000 above budget based on billings through July; and  
 Tuition revenue approximately $632,000 above budget.  
 
Overall, revenues were approximately $2.3 million above budget. Of that amount, $1 million was 
expected to be transferred to the Special Education Trust to offset the special education shortfall, as 
previously approved by the Board of Mayor and Aldermen. The remaining approximately $1.3 million 
would become fund balance and would be available to help address FY27 revenue adjustments when 
those were presented to the Board in October. 
 
Mrs. DeFrancis reported that Food Service would require an approximately $575,000 transfer from the 
General Fund, primarily because of increasing food costs. The District also needed to transfer 
approximately $382,000 for prior-year meal debt, which had already been reflected in the expenditure 
projections. 
 
The Athletics program ended the fiscal year with a positive balance. However, because of the overall 
constraints on the General Fund, the District was unable to pre-purchase FY27 supplies and equipment 
as it had sometimes done in prior years. Necessary purchases would instead be charged to the FY27 
budget. 
 
The majority of federal and state grant funds available during FY26 had been expended, with a portion 
carried forward for summer payroll expenses in July and August and remaining balances carried into 
FY27.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 6 of 11 
 
  
The Special Revenue Fund had a balance of approximately $408,000, representing donations and 
miscellaneous grant balances that would roll forward into the next fiscal year.  
 
Regarding expendable trusts, Mrs. DeFrancis stated that the District ended FY25 with approximately 
$23 million in its trust funds. During the FY26 budget process, approximately $4.5 million was used to 
support revenues, $3.7 million to support expenditures, and $1.5 million for curriculum and 
Chromebooks. Additional transfers included the anticipated $2 million from the Health Trust and 
funding associated with the special education shortfall.  The projected trust fund balance as of June 30, 
2026 was approximately $9.5 million, plus any year-end interest. 
 
Questions and comments included: 
1. Committee Member Turner asked what would constitute a comfortable trust fund balance. Mrs. 
DeFrancis stated that approximately 10% of the District's appropriation would be considered 
comfortable and that the projected $9.5 million balance was below 5%. 
2. Chair O’Connell noted the significant reduction from approximately $23 million the previous 
year and approximately $31 million to $32 million two years earlier, characterizing the rate of 
trust fund use as unsustainable and unhealthy.  
3. Committee Member Potter asked for clarification regarding the use of the prior-year revenue 
surplus to offset FY27 revenue adjustments.  Mrs. DeFrancis explained that the District builds 
its budget using the State's preliminary adequate education estimate provided in November, along 
with estimates for Medicaid, interest, and other revenues. When the tax rate is established, 
however, the District must submit actual and verifiable revenue amounts through its required 
state reporting. 
4. Preliminary information indicated that the FY27 adequate education grant could be lower than 
the amount budgeted, in part because average daily membership and free-and-reduced-price-
meal counts were lower than anticipated. Mrs. DeFrancis explained that free-and-reduced counts 
also affect differentiated aid and the Extraordinary Needs Grant. Final state figures were expected 
by September 1. Once available, administration would report the final revenue difference and the 
proposed method of addressing any shortfall. A portion of the approximately $1.3 million FY26 
revenue surplus could be used for that purpose. 
5. Committee Member Potter summarized that the District was essentially holding the funds in 
reserve against an anticipated FY27 revenue shortfall. Mrs. DeFrancis confirmed that
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 7 of 11 
 
  
assessment. Committee Member Potter expressed disappointment that the funds might be needed 
for that purpose rather than replenishing the District's expendable trusts, particularly given the 
significant use of one-time trust funds in recent years.  
 
On motion of Committee Member Hamer, duly seconded by Committee Member Turner, it was 
moved to approve the Financial Reports as presented and forward this item to the full Board of School 
Committee for approval. All present were in favor and the motion passed. All present were in favor 
and the motion passed. 
 
7.     INFORMATIONAL ITEMS 
(Note:  These items are provided for informational purposes; no action required.)   
 
a. Modular Update – by Kelly Espinola, Assistant Superintendent of High    
Schools and Operations 
 
Dr. Espinola provided an update regarding the District's Priority One construction timeline. She 
reported that a Request for Qualifications (RFQ) had been advertised on July 23 and would close on 
August 25. Following review of qualifications, a Request for Proposals was anticipated to be issued to 
qualified respondents in September.  The initial project contemplated relocating modular classrooms 
from Hillside Middle School to Jewett Street School. The selected contractor would be responsible for 
preparing the receiving site, providing necessary utilities and services, and setting, connecting, and 
commissioning the modular units for occupancy.  Funding for the work had already been incorporated 
into the Priority One project budget. Current estimates indicated that each modular relocation could 
cost approximately $1.8 million, depending on the receiving site and required site preparation. More 
definitive costs would be known following the RFP process.  Following relocation of the Hillside 
modulars, the next anticipated phase was relocation of the Southside modular classrooms to 
Bakersville School.  
 
Questions and comments included: 
1. Committee Member Potter asked how the District selected the schools that would receive 
modulars, particularly given capacity concerns discussed at other schools, including Green 
Acres.  Dr. Espinola stated that the proposed locations were not yet set in stone and could 
change based on occupancy, capacity, and other District needs.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 8 of 11 
 
  
2. Chair O’Connell provided additional background, explaining that the District has six sets of 
modulars. Three sets—at Hillside, Southside, and Beach Street—must be relocated in order for 
the Priority One construction projects to be completed. Modulars at McDonough, McLaughlin, 
and Gossler did not face the same immediate need for relocation, although their long-term 
disposition remained under consideration.  Jewett Street was viewed as an immediate priority 
because of existing space needs. Bakersville was being considered for two primary reasons. 
First, relocating modulars there could allow the District to discontinue use of the Bishop O'Neil 
Center, for which the District was paying approximately $40,000 to $50,000 annually in rent. 
The off-site facility was also considered less than ideal for preschool programming and created 
logistical challenges for families and staff. 
3. The District anticipated continued growth of the dual-language immersion program at 
Bakersville. With three classes per grade and two of those classes associated with dual-
language immersion, additional capacity was expected to be needed.  
4. Committee Member Hamer asked about the timeframe for relocation. The Chair explained that 
Hillside presented the most immediate need. Once the Hillside addition is turned over, 
approximately around or after Christmas 2027, construction work would need to continue in the 
area currently occupied by the modulars. Therefore, the modular relocation would likely need 
to occur during the spring or summer of 2027 so that the new space could be utilized beginning 
in the fall. 
5. Committee Member Potter asked for an update on restoration planning for the area associated 
with the Beach Street project.  Chair O’Connell reported that SMMA had completed a plan that 
was under review by the Department of Public Works. The remedial work was included within 
Harvey Construction's project scope for the new Beach Street School. 
6. Committee Member Potter asked that the planning include a water fountain/water source in the 
park area across from the school, citing the importance of providing children with access to 
water while using the recreational facilities and reducing reliance on plastic bottles and sugary 
beverages.  Chair O’Connell confirmed that at least one water source was included in the 
planning, with the possibility of two, and agreed that the item should continue to be monitored 
as the project advances. Shade was also identified as a consideration.  
 
The Committee received the remaining informational reports, including the professional leave request, 
monthly specialized transportation update, weekly check processing list, and FY27 discussion, without 
further substantive questions.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 9 of 11 
 
  
 
b. Informational Items          
 
● Professional Leave Requests Under $2,000 (see attached report)   
    
● Monthly Specialized Transportation Update – by Cortney    
Medeiros, Director of Transportation 
 
● Weekly Check Processing List       
 
● Fiscal Year 2027 Discussion  
 
The Committee was asked if there were any questions or comments on the above informational items 
that were included in the agenda, which included: the professional leave request, monthly specialized 
transportation update, weekly check processing list, and FY27 discussion.  There were not questions. 
  
   
9.     ADDITIONAL ITEMS   
 
a. Monthly Manifest Signing - Chairman O’Connell is looking for volunteers for this date. 
 
It was stated that two members are already signed up, being Committee Members Turner and Hamer. 
 
b. New Business 
 
Committee Member Hamer requested the transportation facility update that the Committee had 
previously agreed would become a recurring Finance and Facilities agenda item.  Dr. Espinola 
apologized that the update had not been included on the agenda and reported that the District continued 
to search throughout the City for a permanent transportation location. At least one location appeared 
promising.  She had been working with Facilities to begin planning the requirements for a future 
transportation hub, including the appropriate garage height based on the District's largest buses. She 
had also contacted Worcester and obtained an RFP that community had used when seeking a similar 
facility, including provisions relating to a 20-year lease.  In the interim, the District was preparing for 
its move to Candia, scheduled for that Saturday. Administration had contacted bus drivers regarding 
their intentions for September and was determining whether drivers would need shuttle transportation 
to and from Candia. Dr. Espinola indicated that relatively few drivers had expressed interest in using 
such a shuttle.
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 10 of 11 
 
  
 
Committee Member Hamer asked whether there had been movement regarding the potential airport 
location.  Dr. Espinola reported that she had met with airport representatives and toured the proposed 
area, including Lot F, to begin considering the potential placement of the garage, employee vehicles, 
buses, and dispatch office, as well as utility access. Water and electricity were already available. The 
District was awaiting completion of the airport's master-plan process before bringing a formal proposal 
to the Board. Dr. Espinola stated that she did not anticipate that process being completed before 
approximately December. 
 
Committee Member Hamer noted positively that the District was not relying exclusively upon the 
airport option and continued to explore other opportunities that might materialize sooner or prove more 
advantageous. Dr. Espinola confirmed that the District continued to pursue alternatives.  She also 
reported that she was developing a job description for future District transportation mechanics so that 
the District would be prepared should it establish its own transportation hub.  
 
Chair O’Connell requested that the transportation facility update be placed on future agendas, 
recognizing that some monthly updates might be more substantive than others. 
 
Chair O’Connell asked for an update on the introduction of the District's smaller buses and efforts to 
bring specialized transportation routes in-house.  The Administration reported that the District began 
the process during the prior year and successfully brought eight Extended School Year (ESY) routes 
in-house during the summer, resulting in reduced costs. The District would continue bringing routes in-
house where possible while meeting contractual minimum-capacity obligations with existing vendors. 
Administration explained that several transportation vendors had renegotiated contracts using 
standardized rates. Standard-size buses were approximately $525 per bus per day, with larger vehicles 
costing up to approximately $625 per day. Other specialized transportation vendors, following a 3% 
increase, were charging more than $1,000 per bus per day, with monitor costs added separately.  
 
Questions and concerns included: 
1. Chair O’Connell questioned the length of the current vendor contracts and expressed concern that 
long-term contractual commitments limited the District's ability to realize savings by bringing 
transportation services in-house.  He also raised a broader concern regarding the District's
August 12, 2026 Committee on Finance & Facilities 
Page 11 of 11 
 
  
contract-approval process, noting that contracts may be executed after the Board approves the 
underlying concept without the final contract returning to the Board. He suggested that the 
Committee discuss the issue further, potentially with legal counsel, to determine whether 
additional Board review of executed contracts should occur. 
2. He further expressed concern about spending more than $1,000 per day for some student 
transportation services, plus monitor costs, at a time when the District was facing significant 
constraints in funding direct educational positions. 
3. Committee Member Hamer asked how far the District was into the five-year transportation 
contracts. Administration confirmed that Year Two began July 1, 2026.  
 
10.   NON-PUBLIC SESSION 
 
There was no need to go into non-public session. 
 
 
11.  ADJOURNMENT 
 
If there is no further business, a motion is in order to adjourn. 
 
 
On motion of Committee Member Potter, duly seconded by Committee Member Turner, it was moved 
to adjourn.  All were in favor and the meeting adjourned at 6:38 p.m.

Respectfully Submitted, 
  
Clerk of Committee
